title: Imaginary planet
topic: What would my imaginary planet look like?

cards.title: Yellow rock arch on red dunes
cards.text: A lumpy yellow arch capped with pale stone stands on red dunes under a clear blue sky. The first thing to settle is the ground, and the shapes its rock takes.

cards.title: White cliffs over a green valley
cards.text: Three walkers cross bright grass between cliffs left almost white, with their shadows in one flat grey. The rock is drawn with an outline and two tones, nothing more.

cards.title: Picture of the Lake at Hakone
cards.text: A woodblock print in which one steep crag is built from patches of blue, brown, green and yellow. An older way to make rock out of flat colour, where the cliffs above use only two tones.

cards.title: Mountain and River on the Kiso Road
cards.text: Three joined prints of snow-covered mountains along a river, the peaks kept white against blue water and a grey sky. White rock can carry a whole picture, as it does in the valley above.

cards.title: Mound riddled with holes
cards.text: A pale mound pierced with round holes like a sponge, with grey tendrils on its top and a plain blue sky behind. This is rock that looks grown, where the arch looks worn.

cards.title: Orange canyon, one astronaut
cards.text: A comic cover in a single orange: two canyon walls nearly meet above a figure in a white suit, with pale blue distance in the gap. It sent the search towards real places that look like this.

cards.title: First Color Image From Viking Lander 1
cards.text: The first colour picture the Viking 1 lander sent from the surface of Mars: rust-red rocks to the horizon under a pale orange sky. The canyon above is close to the real thing.

cards.title: Io, full disk, from Voyager 1
cards.text: Jupiter's moon Io, put together from frames Voyager 1 took on 4 March 1979: a yellow-green ball blotched with white, orange and black. A real world in colours stranger than any on the board.

cards.title: Mount Vesuvius at Midnight
cards.text: A volcano near Naples throwing red light into a night sky. Io is a moon of volcanoes, and this is how one painter lit a volcano on Earth; the museum says it is not certain he saw the eruption himself.

cards.title: Sand Dunes, Carson Desert, Nevada
cards.text: A photograph of pale dunes with one wagon, the photographer's travelling darkroom, and two sets of footprints. He framed it so the horizon is hidden, and a desert in Nevada reads as another world.

cards.title: Red fan trees on a grey cliff
cards.text: Red trees shaped like open fans lean out from a grey cliff, with one tiny figure in orange on the rock beside them. The second thing to settle is what grows on this planet.

cards.title: Giant mushrooms over clover
cards.text: Two travellers with packs wade through clover-like leaves under grey mushrooms as tall as trees. The plants are ordinary ones made strange only by their size.

cards.title: Pumpkins Used as Dwellings
cards.text: An etching from a set about life on the Moon: its people live in giant pumpkins hung in trees, "to be secure against wild beasts". The oversized plant as a home is an old idea.

cards.title: Lily pads seen from under water
cards.text: Lily pads photographed from below, with the sun breaking through between them and their stems trailing down. It is the view a small traveller would have under giant leaves.

cards.title: Coral tree hung with lanterns
cards.text: A twisted white tree with pink finger-like branches, bound with rope and hung with glowing lanterns, in a green valley under a yellow sky. It grows like coral but stands in open air.

cards.title: Floating blooms on thin stems
cards.text: Red, orange and green blooms like jellyfish and fungi drift on thin curling stems across pale paper. Whether they are plants or animals is left open, which suits a planet nobody has seen.

cards.title: The Marsh Flower, a Sad Human Head
cards.text: A lithograph of a thin plant rising from dark water whose one bloom is a glowing human face. Redon had crossed plant and creature long before the floating blooms above.

cards.title: Vase of Flowers
cards.text: A pastel of red, violet and near-black flowers against yellow and pink, from the last year of the artist's life. Here the flowers are real ones, coloured until they look invented.

cards.title: What colour plants would be elsewhere
cards.text: Works out which light plants would harvest under stars hotter or cooler than the Sun, and so which colours leaves could be. They need not be green.

cards.title: Blue giants and one traveller
cards.text: A watercolour of long-legged blue creatures with many orange eyes stepping past a traveller with a pack, among pink ball-shaped trees. It asks who walks on this planet, and how big they are.

cards.title: Landing capsule under white trunks
cards.text: A small white capsule and a green dome tent sit on red ground under leaning white trunks many times their height. The capsule is what tells you how huge the trunks are.

cards.title: Astronaut beside a split boulder
cards.text: Harrison Schmitt stands next to a huge split boulder on the Moon during Apollo 17, on 13 December 1972; Eugene Cernan took the picture. A real small figure beside a real giant rock.

cards.title: One small figure sets the size
cards.text: Nearly every picture on the planet board has a person, a capsule or an animal a few millimetres tall. Take it out and the rocks and plants could be any size at all.

cards.title: Traveller on pink rubble
cards.text: A traveller with a staff and an orange scarf climbs broken pink stone, and a long-legged machine stands pale in the haze behind. The giant is drawn faint and flat, which makes it far away and large.

cards.title: Shield bearer under a hooded giant
cards.text: A warrior with an oval shield stands among carved stones, and a huge hooded figure with a sword looms pale green in the mist behind. The same device again: the paler the giant, the bigger it feels.

cards.title: Child and cow below a dark hill
cards.text: A child leads a cow along a thin path at the foot of a tall dark green hill with a wooden house on top. One plain hill and a tiny pair give the same feeling of scale without any monster.

cards.title: Pink city of clay towers
cards.text: A lone figure with a sword stands before a crumbling pink city of round towers, stairs and big pots, under a grey sky. Someone built here, so the planet has a past.

cards.title: Flying boat among lilac towers
cards.text: A wooden boat with fins sails the air between lilac towers and domes in a canyon, with blue birds overhead. This city is still lived in, and its people travel by air.

cards.title: The Carriages Used on the Moon
cards.text: An etching of about 1769 whose full title ends "and which move by sails": a wheeled coach on the Moon pulled along by a sail. Transport for another world was being invented long before the flying boat.

cards.title: Ruins of Cliff Dwellings, Cañon de Chelly
cards.text: A photograph of old stone houses tucked under a streaked cliff in Arizona, with horses standing small at its foot. A real ruin that looks as invented as the pink city.

cards.title: Peach sky over a mauve shore
cards.text: A shore of red spires and dark bulb plants beside a grey-mauve sea, under a peach sky with one small pale disc. The mood comes from the sky, so its colour and light are the next thing to settle.

cards.title: Five pastels with their gradients
cards.text: A palette of pale blue, cream, pink, rose and mauve, each shown flat and as a gradient. These are the colours the pink and peach pictures on the planet board keep reaching for.

cards.title: Orange disc with a teal rim
cards.text: A soft glowing disc, orange at the centre and teal at the edge, on a cream ground. It could be this planet's sun, or the planet itself seen from far off.

cards.title: South Wind, Clear Sky
cards.text: The print known as Red Fuji: one mountain in flat red under a sky that deepens to dark blue at the top. A graded sky and a single colour do all the work, as on the shore above.

cards.title: InSight Images a Sunset on Mars
cards.text: The InSight lander photographed the Sun going down on Mars on 25 April 2019: a small white disc in a pale glow over a dark plain. A real sunset on another world, to set beside the invented peach sky.

cards.title: Blue moons and Martian sunsets
cards.text: Explains through the way dust scatters light why the Sun sets blue on Mars, and when our own Moon can look blue. A sky takes its colour from what floats in the air.

cards.title: Earth over the horizon of the Moon
cards.text: Taken from Apollo 8 on 24 December 1968: the Earth rising about five degrees above a grey lunar horizon in a black sky. A sky can hold another world, and no colour of its own.

cards.title: Figure reaching up to a comet
cards.text: A small figure in a long coat raises an arm towards a pale streak falling through a deep blue field. A night sky wants one event in it, and here it is a comet.

cards.title: The Great Comet of 1881
cards.text: A plate from The Trouvelot Astronomical Drawings: the comet as observed on the night of 25 to 26 June 1881, its tail crossing the stars above a dark observatory. A real comet drawn by hand, to go with the pin above.

cards.title: The Planet Jupiter
cards.text: Jupiter as observed on 1 November 1880, from the same set of drawings: grey and cream bands, a pink oval and round black spots. The same hand drawing a whole planet nobody could visit.

cards.title: Everywhere Eyeballs are Aflame
cards.text: A lithograph of a black orb ringed with fire hanging over a dark rocky slope, from a series the museum describes as invented monsters in otherworldly settings. A sky from a dream, made within a few years of the comet plate.

cards.title: Grass combed by the wind
cards.text: Fine green grass lying in waves where the wind has pushed it, photographed close. The last thing to settle is what the planet's surfaces look like from an arm's length away.

cards.title: Sunlight on shallow water
cards.text: Sun bent by ripples into nets of gold and black over a shallow bed. A surface that is all light and no outline, for a lake on this planet or for its sky.

cards.title: Butterfly wing with eye rings
cards.text: A close view of a brown wing with rings of cream, black and pale blue like targets. Markings like these could cover a cliff face or a creature's hide.

cards.title: Grey foam full of dark holes
cards.text: A grey sheet pocked with round black holes spreads across a dark surface, all in black and white. It looks like foam and like a cratered plain at the same time.

cards.title: Photographie Lunaire: Copernic-Képler
cards.text: A plate, its full title ending "Aristarique", from an atlas of the Moon photographed through a telescope at the Paris Observatory: a grey plain pocked with craters. The foam above, at the size of a world.
cards.by: Maurice Loewy and Pierre Henri Puiseaux
cards.credit: Maurice Loewy and Pierre Henri Puiseaux

cards.title: Normal lunar crater
cards.text: A book plate of 1874 showing a ringed crater with a central peak from just above the ground, under a black sky with stars. A close view of the Moon, made nearly a century before anyone stood there.

cards.title: Grainy shoreline in sand and teal
cards.text: A speckled picture in sand, teal, navy and mauve that reads as a coast seen from high above. A small texture and a whole continent can look the same.

cards.title: Sandbars in the Bahamas from orbit
cards.text: A Space Shuttle photograph of March 1994: pale sandbars and tidal channels in bright blue shallows beside the deep dark water of the Tongue of the Ocean. A real coast in the colours of the pin above.

cards.title: Close up and far off look alike
cards.text: Foam, a wing and a coast from orbit share the same blotches and rings. A texture photographed at arm's length can stand in for a whole landscape on the planet.
